title: CHECK constraint
description: A CHECK constraint enforces a rule on every row's values, not just "is it NULL" or "is it unique" - any boolean expression you write. Add a CHECK constraint named `products_price_positive` that requires `products.price` to be greater than 0.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: CHECK constraint
ADD CONSTRAINT <name> CHECK (<boolean expression>) - the expression can reference any column on the table, and Postgres rejects any INSERT or UPDATE that would make it false.
Target the products table, give the constraint the exact name products_price_positive, and write its CHECK condition as price greater than 0.
expected_behavior: products.price is now required to be greater than 0 on every row, present and future.
solution: ALTER TABLE products ADD CONSTRAINT products_price_positive CHECK (price > 0);
explanation: CHECK is the most general constraint type - PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE, and NOT NULL each enforce one specific rule, but CHECK lets you state an arbitrary business rule (price > 0, age >= 0, status IN (...)) directly in the schema.
